What was good in our work of the Medical Corps, that is, in particular, or rather the medical people generally, fortunately there were a few people who had ideas, the strength, and the willingness to actually carry through what they thought of and actually complete what they had envisaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, if I understand you correctly, and again correct me if I'm misstating anything, you seem to be the type that would, at least the military and the local government didn't have any use for that generator because they had plenty of electricity at that point in time, or at least sufficient to cover their needs, which may be one explanation as to why that generator was sitting there all by its lonesome waiting to be plucked by someone like your -- like the hospital.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: You need an answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, yeah. That was a question.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh. As for that generator in particular was concerned, I think that this was the problem: It was in a room in a building that is used for pumping water out for the waterworks. This is a building which is closed otherwise, and no one has the faintest idea what's in there because it is off limits. So you really have to be very fortunate to come across someone who knows that that kind of thing exists there and that you can find that kind of thing out from that person. Secondly, you need to have some kind of technical equipment to transport this because this was very big and very heavy, incredibly big and heavy. Fortunately there was a truck there, a Deutz, and one, two, three, that's how we got the generator. Had I not said "let's," they wouldn't have brought it I'm sure, because really people considered me to be crazy for having initiated like that. Like, "What do we need that for? Look at all of this?" Some of my colleagues reacted that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Doctor, we're not going to waste minutes on this story of the generator, but the main question to be put to you on this is this: If an attack is being prepared, it is only logical that military structures think that the hospital may play an important part in treating wounded, and the military authority must always -- also think that if there is no electricity the hospital might need a generator. Therefore, in the framework of preparing an attack, would it be logical to provide a hospital with a generator? If your generator came before the 9th of May, could this generator be part of a general plan? So all is said is my question. What is your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for that answer, I can present my opinion and this is what it would be, roughly: Had there not been for two people within the medical service who had a bit of the ability to think logically, not soldierly logic because we're not soldiers. Everything that happened in Mostar would have been far worse for the population had those two men not said a lot earlier in 1992 that the Medical Corps at that time in the southern camp next to arms depot, and I said it would be crazy for us to be there because if a shell were to fall then we would explode and your shells, too. And you know what the commander said to me then? He said, "Are you afraid?" So they really did not think along those lines at all, that the staff and the Medical Corps should go underground. Unfortunately the fighters themselves have to remain on the surface or in trenches, in the best possible circumstances. So we could either put the Medical Corps into the cellar of the institute for hygiene, and this was a big-time problem because you had to get approval from the commander and the commander was not happy at all when he heard that we wanted to move from those buildings where he had his troops and that is the southern camp that far away into the centre where the centre -- where the building was sort of a godsend. Well, sort of to be a sort of medical centre. It has different entrances. It's in the right spot. And I always said that is godsend. Why would we be out in a meadow? But we really did have problems. It was very hard for us to carry through what was perfectly logical. I thought throughout, and I still think that this military structure, so to speak, did not think logically. Well, I cannot say medically but in terms of someone who is waging war. I mean, they were not thinking logically either in 1992 and in 1993. And even then on the 9th of May, if you wish. If we had not done what we had done with our own hands and through our own goodwill -- no one helped us. We did not get any help from the military or from the civilian defence to put sandbags on the windows of the hygiene institute. I did that for four days with my technician. I brought in sandbags and put them up on the windows. Nobody helped us. That is sad, to put it mildly. If they expected an attack or if they were planning something -- no. No, no, no. That is simply inconceivable. The two do not go together. A plan and what we did with our own hands, you cannot put the two together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In one word, this generator just came there, got there according to you without, as far as you know, being part of a general plan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No, it was not part of a general plan. If there was a general plan, the generator was just a lucky circumstance for them if they were planning anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Karnavas, you need how much more time?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just a couple questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: As I understand it, somewhere around June 30th, 1993, is when the electricity went out on the east side; is that correct? Somewhere around that period of time?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you allow me to say roughly after that on the 30th there was still electricity, I remember that day because there was still a lot of activity going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And a moment ago, just to pick up on the last question that was asked by the president, you seem to be giving opinions with respect to military logic, you having been trained as a physician. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You weren't -- well --

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. Please let me answer. Not in relation to military logic but some kind of war logic. That's what I said. I don't think I said military. There is a difference. I'm not a military expert, but I watch war movies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And I guess from listening to your answer you're not accusing anybody of using logic. In other words, from what you saw, there were a lot of illogical things going on.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So sometimes you're basing your opinions based on that illogic, perhaps giving credit to those folks that they are indeed logical to start with. If you get my drift.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can this be repeated, because I heard segments of the interpretation so I don't have a full sentence sort of.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, it seems to me that you're trying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, put your question again because it is rather complicated. I myself was a bit lost.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that you're going to put it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll put it in a simple --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I think it would appear, sir, that you're giving credit to some folks within the military structure of actually applying logic to their decisions or actually being logical in themselves. You know, having a clear, logical thinking pattern before doing or carrying out activities?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I heard just now is a question that should be answered by saying no. On the contrary. What I had as my basic opinion then and even now too what was going on from a military point of view and from the point of view of military administration, ideas, if I can call them that way, I don't know what their official name is, very often they are illogical, pointless, not to say stupid sometimes, especially from the point of view of my service, that is to say the Medical Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Exactly that's the point I was trying to make because now we're asking you to sort of read between -- read the tea leaves as to what exactly they were intending to do based on -- on their logic and based on your lack of knowledge and understanding of what they may have been up to. Isn't that what we're doing here right now?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the way I said it was, that for my service, for the Medical Corps, things were not moving along well enough. Why not? Because I think that they were not using their own heads to think as they should have. No one ever asked us anything and, after all, we should know what is relevant as far as our line of work is concerned. We should have been asked for that, and we were taken sort of for granted. There's plenty of doctors. We can always find doctors. That is what always bothered me. It was never raised to the right level of a proper service where you have subordination, where you have to listen to the person who is in charge, especially as far as professional things are concerned. My chief of the Medical Corps was my colleague. I don't think -- I personally don't think that he had completed any kind of military school or had any military knowledge. He was a colleague of mine, a physician.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, based on that last answer it sounds like the command was rather indifferent to the conditions that under which the military doctors such as yourself had to work. Perhaps they should have been listening to you more often and seeking your advice.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were rather indifferent. Especially up until the 9th of May they were rather different, as if we weren't there. From the 9th onwards things were so complex, so difficult, so dangerous that the basic thing was whether you'd reach a certain point alive or not. If you did not, you will end up as a wounded person or as a dying person at the hygiene institute. So that was the most important place in town. It was only after the 9th of May that they realised that that was the most important place in town. By the way, that is one of the very few cellars or basements in town where you can seek shelter, on the eastern side that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir, I want to thank you very much for coming here to give your evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we still have 10 minutes before the break. Who wants to start for 10 minutes and then we can continue after the break. Ms. Nozica, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I'm going to start and then I'm going to continue. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir. I'm just going to ask you a question that is related to the question put by my colleague and then we're going to move on to questions that only pertain to your own line of work, your own profession. Before this conflict, before the 9th of May, where was the war hospital on the east bank? You talked about how the building was found and equipped. How early before the 9th of May did it start functioning that way?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know what I have to tell you? What the most important thing is, the most important problem in relation to my hospital --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Rajkov. My time is limited. I have many subjects.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In your statement, you said that roughly this happened a month before the conflict. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree but that is not going to be a complete and accurate answer. I know what you're going to ask later on.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm not going to ask you anything else in that regard. Please, we have a serious technical problem here. We have to pause between question and answer so that we would not be warned by --

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: The interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It is for the benefit of all the people who do not speak our language. I speak a bit fast, but then please pause before you answer my question. Please, yesterday in response to the questions put bit Honourable Judges you said that you were at a lower rank and that you did not have any contact with doctors from the HVO, the war hospital in Mostar. Am I right? I'm going to ask you that we look at some documents -- you said "yes," but you will have to speak up. Your answer was not recorded. You said "yes," is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. That was the previous question, whether I was at a lower rank and that I didn't have any contacts with my colleagues on the western side. Is that right? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you that we look at certain documents. We will do this rather fast up until the break. In terms of providing medical aid, that is what the HVO gave to the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Mostar. Perhaps you are going to remember some of these medicaments and some much these situations. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can have a look why not.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm going to ask the usher to give the witness the binder with documents that we've prepared for him. 2D 00320 is the document I would like to have on e-court, please. Witness --

utterances.speaker: MS. EGELS
utterances.text: I don't want to interrupt my learned colleague although we have the list the documents weren't released to us until now so would you have a spare copy of these documents, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me tell you, as for hard copies and paper, no. We understood that it was our obligation that we should provide you with documents in electronic form. That is what we've done. I am sorry. We have been preparing this up until the very beginning, so technically speaking we could not have made a paper copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Nozica, just out of courtesy you could have prepared a batch for the Prosecution. When they have documents, they do give you copies, hard copies. I'm going to give them my documents, for the sake of fairness. I'm going to give them my documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there is no need for you to do that. I will provide my own copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I have to tell you, since I have been cautioned, that I was not behaving properly, that most Defence teams do that in electronic form, and we have been doing the same thing as of late. Until now we have been providing hard copies. So the document is 00320.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Sir, you see this order. I think that we all have it in front of us. From Tugomir Gveric, the order from Tugomir Gveric. Have you seen is that? I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So the date is the 6th of June, 1993. The central warehouse of medicaments of the Main Staff of the HZ HB issued an order: "Issue medicaments as requested by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina," and then it says a specific list is attached. "The provided quantities should be sufficient for seven days." Is that right? Is that what is written here? Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it says either accessible or another word; there's two overlapping each other.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now we're going to analyse the medicaments and perhaps you will find this more familiar. 2D 00321 is the document I'm asking for.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note we cannot see any documents at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have been warned that we do not see anything on the ELMO. Sorry, not ELMO but e-court. E-court doesn't seem to be working. I will move on for the sake of saving time because the Prosecutors and the Judges have the documents now.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note we do not have the documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Have you found in?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So this is dated the 8th of June. The war hospital of the HVO of Mostar, the central warehouse HZ HB, and now there is this shipment of medicaments that is prepared for the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Do you remember that this happened roughly around that time? That you perhaps you received this shipment of medicine after this date? You see what this is all about and you will understand it better than I do.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see what this is all about, but that I remember this kind of paper.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Sir, you said and I repeat that you were at a lower level and you did not communicate. I'm asking you whether you remember that the hospital received this kind of quantify of medicine at the time. I'm not asking you whether you saw the document.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. I misunderstood what you were saying. Well, I could conclude that if I find something very specific, that perhaps appeared before my very own eyes then.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Please have a look.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am having a look in detail at that. I cannot give you any guarantees because I do not see any specific medicine or medicament which is something that I would remember having seen with my own eyes. This is regular stuff, antibiotics, and so on and so forth, and Kanesten. That is used in gynaecology. I don't see that it's a very big quantity. If we're talking about medicine boxes it's not too much. I don't know I cannot say yes I can no the say no. There were such medicaments in infirmaries and in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm going to ask if we could move in -- if we could take the break now. I guess that it would be best to resolve the problem of e-court during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... 20-minute break. We'll start back then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Nozica, the interpreters are kindly asking you to slow down because they have a problem following you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: They said also that it is a bigger problem that my question and your answer often overlap and they have asked us to make a pause between my question and your answer. Before the break we looked at the document that is still on the screen, which is a list of medicines dated 8 June, 1993. Tell me, did you know that somebody from the command of the 4th Corps approximately around that time asked from the HVO services amounting to medical assistance starting with medicines, transportation, or any such thing? Did you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally never heard of any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to look at document 2D 00322.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Were you able to locate that document?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: As we can see, this is actually a request by the command of the 4th Corps dated 9 June; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it says in the heading.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And the signature is by Mr. Arif Pasalic. There is no doubt about that, or somebody signed on his behalf, and his name is typed out; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can we look at some important things in this request, and for the transcript I'm going to read them. This is a request. This says in the first sentence, please pay attention: "Considering that you announced through the media that there would be medical cooperation and help to the wounded and sick, we are addressing you with the requirement." My first question is this: Did you hear the time that the Medical Corps of the HVO used the media to announce that they were prepared to extend help to the wounded and sick on the east side?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only thing that might have happened could have been on the radio. I listened to the radio, but I did not hear any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you have any reason to doubt that Mr. Arif Pasalic sent this request based on the announcement on the media regardless of what the source of the announcement was for him at the time?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that was the case, it would be a reasonable act because this was a humanitarian person -- purpose and any course of action was only welcome, and if you ask me, I would have also reacted in the same way.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When we're talking -- I'm waiting for the interpretation. When we are talking about things being reasonable or not, are you talking about the reason of the HVO Medical Corps or the reasoning of Mr. Arif Pasalic who accepted such an assistance with this letter? Who do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: If what we have before us is true, then both would be reasonable things to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And now we shall see what is requested here in this letter. Under 1 it says: "Promptly secure a free and guaranteed passage or change of shift for volunteer surgical teams or pending the agreement team from the city wartime hospital with the protection of International Commission of the Red Cross and UNPROFOR." Is that correct? The second item I'm not going to go through everything because you have the document before you so you can read for yourself the things I don't read aloud. "We are kindly asking of you to deliver a list of medicines and medical supplies." And the third request: "Since we have one ambulance, we are kindly asking you to provide us with two ambulances or please return to us the medical vehicle Mercedes diesel that was taken from us." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm laughing because I know exactly which Mercedes is in question. It had the Mostar licence plate.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Are you in doubt this is not a Mostar document?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me wait for the interpretation. It says "Mostar." In Mostar I suppose this is what they did, but I suppose that it is about Mostar. I know -- I just happened to know about the Mercedes. I know when this Mercedes was taken from us.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let me just remind you and ask you to pay attention to whom the letter is addressed. It says the HVO medical headquarters for the commander of the HVO Mostar wartime hospital. Would you agree that both were in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Medical Corps of the HVO, it would be logical that it was in Mostar, whereas the war hospital of the HVO is the hospital that used to be called Safet Mujic hospital, and then it was transformed into the HVO war hospital at the beginning of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And it was in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can we look at the answer of the chief of the Medical Corps dated 11/6. 2D 00323 is the number of the document. The date is 11 June. Can we look at that answer together, please? Have you found it? 323 is the number.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Again, Defence Department, the Medical Corps and the answer is dated 11 June. It says "regarding the request of the command of the 4th Corps," and reference is made to the previous document, "we are duty-bound to answer the delivery of the list of medicines and medical supplies is being drafted. The medical supplies are ready and waiting for transport to the left bank by the assistance of UNPROFOR. As to your request for ambulance vehicles, we have to remind you that during the aggression against the city of Mostar you destroyed 19 ambulance vehicles, wounding six drivers and killing one. We're not able to comply with your request even though we would like to do so, because we ourselves do not have enough vehicles." Further down there is an offer. I would like to know whether you've ever heard of this offer. This is very important. The first thing it says regarding the team of doctors, specialists, which you are requesting: "We have to inform you that there are no volunteers among the Muslim staff." And the next sentence, please. "Since the conditions for the care of the civilians and soldiers on our side are much better than yours, we hereby ask you for the umpteenth time to send all your wounded and sick to the HVO war hospital where they will enjoy the same treatment as our soldiers in keeping with the Hippocratic Oath and ethics. The Main Staff of the HVO Medical Corps, and I personally guarantee that the equal treatment will be provided." Mr. Rajkov, did you ever hear that such a proposal was put to your hospital and the wounded who were treated there? And when you say your hospital, I also imply all the other facilities that existed. Did you ever hear of such a proposal?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: To our hospital or our patients, no. For example, not me. If by saying "my hospital" you're implying my colleagues and the patients, that we ever heard of that or that our patients ever heard of that, my answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Of course you can answer for yourself, but can you guarantee that the chief administrator of your hospital didn't hear that?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot guarantee for the chief administrator of my hospital. I never spoke of anything with him. Not even such a slight segment of such an offer a transfer of patients across the river because such an offer was on the table. I never heard any such thing from had him, anything in that sense. We never discussed any such thing. We never discussed anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I can also conclude based on your answer that you didn't know that the 4th Corps sent a request for some medicines. You have also told us that the quantities of drugs that arrived, you were not aware of and that they might have arrived from the western side of Mostar. Would you agree with me that all that arrived from the -- that arrived in terms of medical supplies and equipment arrived with the help of international organisations? Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: What we received by way of medical supplies, equipment, and medicines for the most part came through various international medical organisations, and it was either done on purpose or by accident. Like it happened once that a lorry stopped in front of the building although everything was intended for Jablanica. So one-third of the load was unloaded for us, which was lucky for us. And the rest of the supplies came from civilians, from the ruins. Everything that was of medical nature ended up at the hospital. Where else would it have ended?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It seems that we're working so well with these pauses that the interpreters do not have a problem, and I don't know whether I'm going to have a problem, whether I'm going to be able to finish what I plan to do. Do you know why I asked you this? In one of these documents it says, and a certain number of witnesses were heard before this Trial Chamber, I would like to remind the Trial Chamber these were some of the observers who were heard, say, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: (redacted), I'm going to talk about that, which did indeed come as aid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you please issue an order to erase line 7 on page 19 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to Your Honours. I thought that this would in no way reveal the identity of these witnesses, because I did not refer to any names.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So do we have information that certain quantities of medical aid were brought in, or blood as well in addition to medicaments? I'm trying to say that you did not inevitably have to know that what an international organisation was bringing in was coming from the western bank. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is right that I cannot know from where something had left and which way it went.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have a look at two other documents that speak of that precisely? Again these are lists of medicaments. 2D 00325. Tell me when you find it so we don't have to wait for e-court.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is the 15th of May, 1993. The HVO war hospital in Mostar, the central warehouse of medical equipment of the HZ HB, a shipment to the BH army. I don't know whether there's anything special here. I'm just going to ask you whether you remember whether there were shortages at the time and whether you received any such medicine at the time from anyone. Can you remember any such thing? One hundred pieces, I think you may remember something like that.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, remember. If they're referring to what we will called "brown nilej" [phoen], then it's nothing special. Were it some kind of a device, then perhaps I could recognise it. Again, I have to tell you the same thing. I'm sorry that I cannot be of assistance to you, but nothing is that special for me to be able to say, Aha, that is what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. You're not assisting me, you're assisting the truth.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: There are going to be witnesses who can confirm what you cannot remember. I'm just asking about what you know. Can we just have a look at 2D 00328. Mr. Rajkov, you know, yesterday two Honourable Judges asked you about whether there was this kind of cooperation or any kind of input from the Croatian side at the time of the conflict, and since we have some documentation we are trying to refresh your memory, if you can remember any of this. I'm not bringing any pressure to bear on you, no. Have you found the document?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: As I mentioned a few moments ago how this went and what witnesses confirmed this, well, you just tell me if you remember this. It's blood after all. The 25th of September. See? It says here that it went through the UNHCR. Do you remember that roughly?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you why I don't remember this. I do not remember this because no matter how strange it may seem there was too much work for me to be able to go upstairs that often where there was an alleged transfusion service. I'm saying alleged because they would -- they were just working on a give-and-take blood basis. I went there very rarely. However, blood as therapy, if I can put it this way, in that hospital it was only one doctor who was in charge of that. That was the only true professional among us at the time, because the rest of us were GPs and there was one dentist, and we would not have dared do it just like that. So it's only one person who can know about that. That is the head of the hospital at the time, who was my boss at the time, Dr. Miljevic, who was the person in charge, and he's the only person who can remember that. I don't know of any such thing. He was an anaesthesiologist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday I asked you this for the precise reason. I am asking questions. I don't need any documents. I know the problems with blood. And when I asked about the cooperation you said that at your level you didn't know anything about cooperation. I even asked you without knowing the documents, I don't need documents, as I say, to ask my questions. I asked you about the transfusion of blood and if you had any problems. You explained to us what you had done. I know that when you carry out a surgical procedure you need blood. Yesterday, we saw a document that pertains to the month of September, and according to that document the UNHCR received blood, and it seems that it was for your hospital, and you are saying that you don't know anything that -- that it was the HVO or the UNHCR and my hospital were involved in all that. When you were in the OR, when you needed blood for the transfusion for your patient, you didn't know where the blood came from, would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. In actual fact I didn't know where the blood was coming from. Primarily it was coming from our, again I'm saying alleged transfusiology. It's a small room. Now, where the blood came from, where it reached that room, that is beyond my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence has now shown us a number of documents that establish apparently that the HVO did supply your medical unit with blood material, masks, gloves, antibiotics, and so on and so forth. The discovery that you can base on these documents, what would be your conclusion? We are -- what would be your conclusion based on the documents that have just been shown to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you're asking for a conclusion on the basis of what was presented to me today and which I should take as the truth that this happened in actual fact, that these were not only attempts. This may be a paper showing intention, but, let's say, it wasn't carried through, what I can say is well done, praiseworthy, but these are five doses of blood, for instance, AB positive and B positive. Five doses of blood perhaps for one moment, two patients. Was there more of that and what the amount was? I don't know. I don't have the documents in front of me. As to what I saw beforehand, it is not that much. A hospital with that much patients uses up a lot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We discovered yesterday there were international doctors, foreign doctors who helped you, people from Spain and so on and so forth. As doctors of various specialties, they could also have their own supplies. I suppose that Medecins sans Frontieres who came to your hospital, if they had a problem they could turn to their own supplies. Did foreign medical teams have such resources and were they of any value to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If they hear this I don't want them to be offended. I'm just saying that there were two few of us. Then as professionals in certain specialties that we were -- that we did not have enough of, like anaesthesiology, then as far as medicaments were concerned and material, as far as I managed to notice they could not bring in quantities that would be sufficient, that would be satisfactory. I don't know why. I had the impression that they were not allowed to bring in more than they would carry in one bag. So they brought in some special things, if I can put it that way. You'd hardly see a physician coming in followed by a truck of material, no. But every one of them tried to bring something in based on information he had received from his predecessor, what was lacking and what would be lacking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please carry on, Ms. Nozica. Perhaps you can carry on to another subject. There may be other interesting subjects.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. Precisely that's what I've prepared for this very short time and in relation to what the witness said. These are small quantities. With this very short time with the witness, unfortunately we cannot go through all the documentation we have but we are going to do it some other time.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now I'd just like to move on to a subject that you perhaps knew nothing of, cooperation between the two. I keep that in mind all the time. With some documents I'll try to jog your memory. Perhaps you will remember at least something that constitutes cooperation. Can we have a look at 2D 00319?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: 319. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's ahead. I have to have a look.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes. It's at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Please, now you have it here. It's very short. You see it's the 6th of May; right? Quite an important date. Did you have any contact with the war hospital in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to ask you what period you're asking me about.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The time that this document refers to. That is the month of May.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 6th of May, 1993. Officially, no. We in the hygiene institute, that we had contacts with the hospital in Jablanica? No. But I personally know the doctors who were on duty in Jablanica at that time. I know that they went there for a certain period of time and would rotate in shifts. That's why I know that they were there.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: At that time again, do you know who Mr. Ivan Bagaric was?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: He signed this document as assistant to head of defence department sector for health care.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what's written here.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I must say I'm surprised you haven't heard of him. This document speaks of - could you have a look at the document - of appointing a certain surgical team for work at the Jablanica wartime hospital. Four names are mentioned, and it was said that the team would replace a surgical team at the Jablanica wartime hospital who will return to Mostar, to the Mostar regional wartime hospital, and that team consists of, and then three names. Did you know these doctors? Did you know that this is how these doctors went there, to work?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew about Jablanica. I already told you these teams went there, three or four persons per shift. Dr. Hajdarevic, Dr. Saric were there at that time in Jablanica. They stayed there during the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could we now look at 2D 00333.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: 333. Green or blue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Nozica, with regard to the document we've just talked about with the Jablanica team which is about to be transferred to the Mostar regional wartime hospital, the Mostar regional hospital, is that the HVO or the ABiH hospital?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't know whether the interpretation I got is right, but it's the other way around. The wartime hospital in Mostar. I thought it was obvious, because the letter is signed by the assistant to head of defence department sector for health care, Dr. Ivan Bagaric. So the team went from the wartime hospital to Jablanica to replace doctors from the HVO hospital in Mostar yet again. So all of these people are from the HVO wartime hospital in Mostar who are taking turns in the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina hospital.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why is this issue relevant to the witness, because he's from the ABiH? If the document were to say that these doctors are going to go to the ABiH wartime hospital, I would have understood, but my feeling is these are doctors working only for the HVO. So what's the relevance?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The problem is in the interpretation that you're getting. Twice I've already said that the wartime hospital in Jablanica is a hospital of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. That's what I asked the witness about, and that is what the witness confirmed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I intervene? May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please, enlighten us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What was the number? What was the number of the document?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time when Dr. Taslaman or Dr. Safet Omerovic were appointed to be the replacement for the surgical team that was working at that time in Jablanica, and that is Dr. Hajdarevic and Dr. Saric. Let me say quite sincerely I don't know whether that town was in the state of fighting between the two sides on that day earlier or later. I just know that that was the regular shift of the staff that was employed in the HVO hospital. These are regular employees with salaries, and that was the usual circulation from earlier on. That had already been happening from earlier on, and I know that this shift did not manage to come in due to something. That is to say something happened during the conflict, so they could not replace Dr. Hajdarevic and Dr. Saric. They stayed on throughout that period one year in Jablanica even longer than that. Something happened in Jablanica which prevented the replacement from being effected, but both are employees of the HVO, and I don't know whether the Jablanica hospital can be considered the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina hospital at the time. Part of the HVO hospital is how I regarded it at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Sir, the 6th of May is the day when you remained on the eastern side.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 6th of May I was on duty, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The 9th of May is the day when you say that the attack started by the HVO against the eastern side.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I'm not the only one.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I am now conducting this examination with you. This document is dated the 6th of May. Can you agree and can you give the same kind of answer that you gave to Mr. Karnavas that everything that looks like the preparation of the eastern side for a future conflict was not felt at all by the doctors and the medical staff? That's what you said; right? You didn't know anything about that, and you believe that there was no preparation for that?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can we conclude on the basis of this document that the wartime hospital of the HVO Mostar did not know anything about the conflict to come, because on the 6th of May they sent four doctors as a shift to work in Jablanica, and they were replacing three, and they're all ethnic Muslims. Unfortunately we have to speak in those terms.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I didn't really pay attention to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Except for Djuro Grumic he's a nurse. Can we conclude that your colleagues on the western bank likewise did not know about this just like you didn't? Just say yes or no and let's move on. I haven't got much time, and I really would like to deal with --

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: My conclusion is that the situation was as usual from their point of view since they were carrying out these regular replacements.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. That's why I showed this document. Now, for instance, you're going to look at two documents that refer to cooperation. 2D 00333. 2D 00333.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We thought that we have a technical problem, but we don't. Could you please read this. To keep things as short of possible, did you know Ms. Sally Becker?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, please put the question by saying this document raises the issue of a document being sent at issue and then put your question, because if you ask him to read the document, you wait for him to read the document, and then you put the question. That's a waste of time. He has read the document. He can see it. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you. That's exactly what I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Does the witness know Ms. Sally Becker at all and then perhaps he could know something about that. Do you know this lady, and do you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Ms. Sally Becker. I mean I knew her. I wonder if I could recognise her now. I knew her for quit a while in terms of days, a certain number of days. It seemed like a very long time to me. She was in the hygiene institute. She would usually sleep on the bed next to mine. I remember her.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the document, about cars?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that she managed to take out any medical things.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You don't seem to have a very good experience or good opinion of her help.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not of her medical help.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can we now look at another document, 2D 00327, another document about medical cooperation. Did you find it?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is a very important document. This is another request sent by the Defence department on the 16th of September. As the Presiding Judge said, the 16th of September is a very important date and this was September to the UNPROFOR to the Spanish Battalion. It was sent by deputy head of the medical didn't, Mr. Ivan Bagaric. Somebody the signed the letter on his behalf. Again in this request -- you're reading it. Please take some time to read the document.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to read it out loud?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: No. Read it to yourself.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it; I'm a fast reader.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Again at this request, it is requested from the Spanish Battalion to mediate in the offer to the Muslim side for the accommodation and treatment, and I quote that, "especially women and children in that hospital in Mostar." Again, they're going getting the same equal treatment, and I remind you this was said in the previous document 2D 00323 dated 11 June 1993. And another interesting thing is the following sentence, the last sentence actually?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: "We do this for one single reason which is a humanitarian reason and we are kindly asking you not to give any political connotation to this request." First of all, did you know anything about this? And the last sentence in this document, does it show the humanitarian nature that your colleagues on the western side obviously had and displayed when it came to the treatment of all people regardless of their ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document itself and its contents or that something was implemented based on those document I don't know. The last sentence sounds really nice and it has been worded really very well. Chapeau.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petkovic and Mr. Praljak still have to put their questions. We have another 45 minutes to go. So did you agree as to the questions and as to the time? Because you've used already over 40 minutes. Don't forget you've got your colleagues as well. Ms. Alaburic, how many minutes do you need?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mrs. Nozica has consulted us, and we believe that documents that she's trying to have admitted are very important and that's why General Petkovic's Defence has given part of its time to our colleague Nozica, so you needn't worry. We have redistributed the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you said you have given ought your time or not? Ms. Alaburic, do you need a few minutes thereafter.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have given part of the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely how many minutes do you need.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ten minutes at the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So ten minutes to you. Mr. Kovacic on behalf of Mr. Praljak, how much time do you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it would be ideal that we have up to 15 minutes for Mr. Praljak and Ms. Pinter will need two or three minutes for the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, so if I added all up Ms. Alaburic and Mr. Kovacic that's about 30 minutes. So Ms. Nozica, you have another 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I'll try and accomplish everything within that time or at least the most important part of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We've heard your answer. We can move on to the next topic. Unfortunately, when it comes to what the Judges asked you, that is the evacuation of the ill, the wounded, even the soldiers of the BH army, I have prepared a few documents but unfortunately I'll be able to show you just one much them because unfortunately we don't have enough time. The document is 2D 00326. Can you please look at that document. Did you find it?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It has two pages.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The date is 10 September 1993, and yes, it does have two pages. And this is a list of wounded members of the BiH army, which was -- which were sent from the war hospital of the HVO Mostar to the hospital in Split. Did you know anything about this? Does any name ring a bell? Does any name remind you of somebody, kind of jog your memory? From Mostar people were transferred to Split because Split could probably could have provided them with better treatment than the HVO hospital in Mostar. Do you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know, but I'm trying to find a familiar name among the many names.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. You don't know. We can move on. Let's not dwell upon this. I'm going to find witnesses who will be able to confirm this document for us. Do you know anything about the number of people who died in the month of May and were members of the HVO? In the month of May 1993, how many were killed on the western bank? How many were wounded, how many were killed on the western bank? Do you have any perception of those numbers?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't even know how many were killed on my side. I know the number of wounded, but I don't know the number of those who died, who were killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can we look at the document P 02445. This is a Prosecutor's document. You must have it in your binder, sir, here.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you read number again?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: P 02445. It's at the very beginning amongst the documents in the binder.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you find it? We can look at it together just briefly. The date is 18 May. It's another list of dead and wounded. And can we move on to the last page of this document, of its B/C/S version, the last page of the document. Also the last page in the English. You can look at it on the screen. On that date, the 18th of May, there were 245 wounded by then, and there is the breakdown by ethnic background. Fifty-five wounded civilians, 35 dead soldiers, Croats, and 2 Muslims, and out of 15 dead civilians there were 13 Muslims, and in the morgue there were 8 unidentified persons. Do you have any doubt -- do you have any reason to doubt these numbers? Are these numbers correct, according to you?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why would I doubt about the accuracy of an official document? This is an official document. There's no stamp or any such thing, but --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is an official document.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it's an official document, then it should abide by certain rules. I don't know whether the stamp on the document is the Tribunal's stamp.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The document contains all the names, and it is a document which is a Prosecution exhibit. Did you know that there were exchanges of prisoners, members of the BiH army and the HVO during the time when you worked at the hospital? Did you ever hear of anybody having been exchanged, of any exchanges that were taking place? During the period of time that you were practising in the hospital in September, did you ever receive any exchanged members of the BiH army who had need for medical assistance?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were patients who were discharged from my hospital and went to the other side. They were mostly HVO prisoners who were wounded, who were surgically treated at our hospital and then were transported to the other side. Whether they were exchanged or were just transported or were they exchanged for another group of people at the same moment, I wouldn't be sure and I can't tell you that they were exchanged. Whether there were any patients wounded and if this is the segment you're asking me about from the other side, I don't remember them coming as a group. I know that people did come from the other side, especially ones that were released from various camps.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: From various camps on both sides?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the camps on the western side.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And what was the name of that on the eastern side? Where were the Croatian prisoners kept on the eastern side?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: What the name was?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me about the name of the prison? It was a prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can we look at 2D 00315?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please. I need a few moments. Please registrar, can we move to private session just for a few seconds.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just for the record --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: While we are talking about this document, could you inform the Chamber, Ms. Nozica, on how this was compiled? What is the basis for this list? Is it a list which covers corpses found on both sides of the Neretva, or is it limited to casualties in the area controlled by HVO?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, since the list was put together on the 18th of May, 1993, it would be logical that at the time it could have only comprised those persons that were killed or wounded on the side that was under the control of the HVO. That would be logical. We are still waiting for 2D 00315.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: But you have got it, and the subject of this document is an evacuation. You had the time to look at it. The transport was done through the Spanish Battalion, and it says: "With the help of the APCs of the Spanish Battalion, the wounded were transferred to our hospital. In turn, the HVO has given to the Muslim side five wounded members of the MOS who had been treated at the war hospital in Mostar. The wounded members of the HVO, I took over on the left side directly from the prison." Further on what is described is the condition of the people and everything that accompanied the evacuation. And finally it is said that future evacuations are to be expected and also that UNPROFOR is expected to help further evacuations. Would you agree with me that the evacuations were impossible at the time without the help of UNPROFOR and other international organisations?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say that they were almost impossible. They were absolutely impossible.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I don't have much more time, and I have a very important thing. I have a document that was signed by you personally. It -- do you know that a trial is ongoing in Mostar against some members of the BH army for war crimes committed in the prisons where Croats were kept during the war?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there was a trial. I don't know whether there is a new one or whether that trial still continues.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The person -- the accused is Mr. Cupina who is the first accused in that trial. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about that. This is the trial that I had in mind, and I thought that it was finished.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes, it was finished. Do you know how it ended and when it ended?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It must have been a year.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Just for the record, it ended yesterday with the first instance decision by which eight accused have been sentenced a to total of 18 years in prison, and they were all members of the BiH army who were either wardens or were in anyway involved with the prisons where members of the HVO were kept. I'm now going to ask you something, and at the beginning I would like to say this to avoid any misunderstandings, in this case I don't have the time to show you all the documents, did you know anything, and I'm not pointing my finger at you in any way, Mr. Rajkov because the documents are not pointing at you, but I'm asking you, did you know that the members of the HVO who were incarcerated on the 30th June 1993 and remained in prison until the month of March in 1994 were forced to give blood without their consent?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that prisoners or detainees, the HVO detainees as they were defined in the protocol, did arrive at the hospital to give blood amongst other things. As a matter of principle, I would like to say that they would normally give blood to their own colleagues because they were all brought to our hospital and were treated by us. As for them being forced to give blood against their own will, I must say that transfusion was on the upper floor and it may seem strange to you in -- in peacetimes it may be possible to know what's going on, but in wartimes, and I was working for 20 hours, I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You didn't know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know anything about people giving blood by force. I know that they did come, that they did give blood mostly to their colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Why to their colleagues? What was the situation of their colleagues? Why did they need blood? Were they wounded? Were they wounded as a labour force on the first lines? Were they ill-treated in prisons? Why did they need blood? Why did they need transfusions?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some serious wounds. I remember a few patients. I operated on some of them together with my colleagues. They sustained explosive wounds, shell wounds. I remember a patient Josip Kordic, Jakov Raspudic, and some others who had been hit by shells, or stepped on a mine in front of the SDK building in the main street, on Titova Street. There were a lot of wounded people on that day. I don't know what day it was but I still remember the event, the incident.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What did HVO prisoners do on the street on that day? Did you know that they were being taken to work on the front line, that they were being taken to do some engineering works on the front line or on the separation line between the HVO and the BiH army?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know from some conversations when I asked how many -- how some that there were so many of them there, there were a lot of them in that group of wounded, wounded prisoners. As far as I can remember know it arose that at that time they were helping with the loading or unloading of something, some lorries carrying humanitarian aid, flour, or what, and they were transporting that to some depots.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you ever hear that some of the prisoners -- I know that my time is almost up, I'm going to have just a couple of questions about two important documents. Did you ever hear that one of the prisoners or some of the Croatian prisoners were so badly beaten that they succumbed to their wounds as a result of the beating? Did you ever come into contact with any such patients as a doctor?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never came in contact with that type of wounds or injuries.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And now just one more question. We'll go back to a document, and let me ask you this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please conclude. Please conclude.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... drawing my examination to an end.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In a protocol if you had a column and I'm referring you to Exhibit 9672 under which you recorded the place of death or wounding, and you put Santiceva. What did that mean what did Santiceva mean for you? Was that the front line?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you have Santiceva in the protocol, this is probably -- I apologise, not probably I apologise this was the area along the Santiceva street --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- along its entirely length but not along the front line. Its entirety length some 200 or 300 metres behind Santiceva in the direction of the Neretva River and this is for the sake of the protocol.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Just for the sake of the protocol?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for the sake of the protocol from Santiceva to the Neretva.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And now the last document 2D 00335.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please slow down for the interpreters and the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is a death certificate that you signed yourself 2D 00 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, my colleagues are telling me that you have used all the time you had at your disposal.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I know that, but I can ask questions because the time was given to me by my colleague sitting behind me and only about this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're taking her time.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that this document is very relevant and this is a document that was signed by the witness. I believe that the question will also be relevant.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you find the document?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Is this your signature?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can we look at the document together? Mario Vasic [as interpreted], is that the name?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Another name, the time of death is 22nd September 1993, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Does it say SDK here as the place of death?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you please tell me, what does it mean, SDK, when it says the cause of death in Bosnian. It hasn't been translated. I was not sure this is your translation. Does it mean contusion, head contusion?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes this is a translation of a forensic medical term.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is what you recorded?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In view of the wound, what did he die of on the 22nd of September, 1993? What did the patient die of? Where did he die? And as the result of what?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Such a diagnosis --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Doesn't this diagnosis mean that he was hit by something?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: This means that the wound was a result of a hit with a blunt thing. It could have been a stone falling from a building or the axe.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I have no further questions, sir. We'll elaborated that -- elaborate this in writing. We will establish that the patient had been beaten and that he was brought to you dead for the purpose of you issuing a certificate of his death.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just 15 seconds more doctor. We have just seen a document in which you stated in Latin contusio capitis, and you said that his head had been smashed. You did not attempt to find out how a soldier because apparently he was an HVO soldier, how his head was hit or smashed in the ABiH sector?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I personally never inquired about circumstances involved when cause of death is concerned. They used me for cause of death and signing death certificates for a very simple reason. I am the only one in the hospital who had that kind of stamp, that kind of seal, so I was the own one who could verify it with a seal. So if I'm not to say all but practically all death certificates issued in the hospital, especially such for HVO prisoners that went elsewhere were signed by me. I knew that some day somebody would ask me something about that. As for the circumstances involved, I did not go into that. It was for me to establish what the main wound was and what was the cause of death and to confirm that the said person was dead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Next counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Beginning Your Honours. Good evening Dr. Rajkov. On behalf of the Defence of General Praljak, I would like to put a question to you with regard to a document, 3D 00378. Today in response -- you'll get it you'll get the document. Today in response to a friend [as interpreted] put by my colleagues from the Prosecution, line 24, page 3, you mentioned your colleague Dr. Mira Candzic.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Candzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Could you just give us her name, Candzic?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Camdzic, Almira Camdzic with an M not an N.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: The doctor was wounded?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Her right leg was amputated and she had wounds in the abdomen; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you to have a look at this document that's in front of you.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: And tell us whether this is precisely Dr. Camdzic.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not very legible.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Yes. In your statement you also know that she had been evacuated.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: So you would agree with me that this document shows that General Praljak ensured a helicopter for Dr. Camdzic to be taken to Split?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what's written here.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: The last question on my part: Dr. Camdzic was a Bosniak, a Muslim; right?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now General Praljak, with the leave of the Court, is going to take over. Cross-examination by the Accused Praljak:

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, Dr. Rajkov.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good evening.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: We have very little time so please answer me as briefly as possible. The military hospital on the fence, where could it be seen from if you're outside, if you're out of that street, say, on the right-hand side? Could it be seen anywhere except 5 -- 50 metres left or right? Just say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you get out of the street, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Now let us go back to the generator. The generators were used -- well, you tell me if you don't agree with me.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Water is obtained through pumps when there is electricity. When there is a power cut, the generator is automatically switched on like in the hospital so there would be water even when there is no electricity. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's logical.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: When the generator was taken from the pump and when there was no electricity, then there could no longer be any water in the area that was serviced by that pump station. Is that logical?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's logical if that was its purpose.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please, on page -- or, rather, do you know that near your hospital, behind your hospital there was a mortar position of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina? Do you know that? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Wait a minute, because this is a relevant question which is raised by General Praljak. You said you didn't know. You didn't know because you didn't get out or didn't know what happened? When you were going around in the surroundings you never happened to see any mortar position. Can you catch the difference? What can you say, to be more clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never saw anything that would look like that kind of a war position, a mortar position or a machine-gun nest or anything like that near the building. Behind the building is a little hill and some small family homes. I didn't go into the houses and the yards, but behind the institute itself I would have seen that. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: And you don't know about the little hill?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: What happened among the houses and the hills I cannot guarantee.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Nika, could you please put that map down? Oh. Would you please take care of that map? Now I'm going to ask you the following: In your statement, on page 6 you say for that day, the 9th, "in view of the fact that the HVO was in northern camp, which was near us, I was afraid that the HVO would knock at our door any moment." This is a very accurate map of Mostar. Please mark the building of your hospital and of the northern camp.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this? It's like a satellite image or something.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Exactly. You can see where your hospital is and you can see where the northern camp is.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. I have never really seen any such thing from the air.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: All right. While you're orienting yourself --

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: You say the northern camp was near our hospital; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters cannot hear the witness. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: You were afraid that the HVO would knock at your door.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters can still not hear the witness. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Yes. We have "yes" registered as your answer in terms of the first question. You were afraid that the HVO would knock at your door. The answer was yes.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
