utterances.text: Now, what we all know, logic, logic, minimal logic. In war and peace, it's always the same. If anyone from the HVO was planning that action of attacking Mostar, if anyone did that, I don't know, wouldn't it have been logical to attack from the northern camp and to cut off at least that part of Mostar where you were, where the railway station was, and so on? In your view, would that not have been logical?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. Viewed from the point of view of war, it would be good.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: All right. The left side and the right side --

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what it looks like to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: As you know or, rather, do you know that anyone from the northern camp attacked anyone over there? Do you know on that day, the 9th of May? Did they move towards you? Did they shoot at you?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did shoot, but that they launched an attack, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now please mark where your hospital was. Mark the northern camp.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters cannot hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You want me to put a circle round it? THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Yes, yes. And please mark your hospital as number 1, northern camp number 2.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness is inaudible to the interpreters. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Please put a circle around it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We cannot hear the witness again. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Please, just put an arrow and write N, north, and mark the east with E.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: North should be here, so this should be roughly in this direction.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Well, you know where north is so just do it right.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: North and east. This is it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Please take -- mark Musala number 3. You know what Musala is?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Number 3. I just have two more things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is Musala, Mr. Praljak? THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] That is the central part of Mostar. When you go through Tito's bridge to the east side there is a relatively big square, as far as Mostar is concerned. So the central part of Mostar is called Musala. And then this Musala has access to where the fire brigade building was and the Razvitak building, and the street of Marsal Tito.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajkov is what I said right?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes it is attached to the street of Marsal Tito.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: You have marked that with number 3?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the figure is this figure.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Please, you said two big hits at the hospital. One came from the front side, but one came from the north-east, and -- now, this is my question: When you stood at where that hit was and when you looked at the direction in which it had come from, in that direction were -- is that where the HVO artillery positions were? To the best of your knowledge, could that have come from the positions held by HVO artillery, this one hit here that you were talking about?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're talking about the north?

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: You said north-east.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. I said north-east because the building has an entire side. It's not just one point. So north-east would not be in the middle. It would be sort of east. So that's why I said north-east. Now, as I was looking through this hole, I know I see the railway station and in that direction the northern came many and further on the hills that are on the right bank of the Neretva. As for where the artillery of the HVO is or the Croatian artillery, I was not crazy enough to look in that direction where the shelling was coming from.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Thank you. So -- thank you for this information, what it was you saw on the other bank of the Neretva River. On page 11 of your statement you said in the second paragraph, second paragraph, that in the diagnosis it said that they were wounded by sniper shooting. How can a doctor make a distinction between a bullet from a sniper rifle and a bullet fired from a rifle that does not have that kind of sight? Can you make a distinction?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not by the wound.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Thank you. One more thing now. Could you please put this on the ELMO, sir, for the gentleman?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you like to have a number for that map, Mr. Praljak? THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, at the end. At the end, Your Honour. At the end.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Please, on page 5 of your statement, that's the last thing I have to say, you say another case was of when Vedran Dejanic was crossing from the western to the eastern side via Tito's bridge. The sentence is: "He was hit in the head from a sniper near the Neretva River near the Supermarket." Please look at what I drew, this little piece of paper. Please take a look at that.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. I can find my way. I know what it was you were trying to draw.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Can you please mark on this little piece of paper next to the supermarket roughly the place where you claim that this gentleman was killed, Mr. Vedran Dejanic, killed by a sniper shot.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can mark the place exactly. And if this were an enlarged aerial image it would have an accurate picture. But yours, that is an approximation, and I will try to be accurate. It is this right here right here. Now why am I saying that? Because he was lying underneath a lamp, a street lamp that was on a wire on the street in the very middle.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Put a number 1 on there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Please sign that for me and put the date on both documents, and that is all that I ask you to do. This is practice of this court.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, is it? Well, if it is, then what should I use to do it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 25th of January, 2007, and sign, please. First a number for this document. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] And the big map, please. Could that be signed too?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, let's start with this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Somebody should write this out very specifically: Sketch drawn by Mr. Praljak; number 1 put by Dr. Rajkov.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please just put the signature there for me. Don't be afraid, Doctor.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The drawing prepared by General Praljak and marked in court by the witness shall be given IC 253, Your Honours. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] An IC number for the map too, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the map please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And the map also marked by the witness in court shall be given Exhibit Number IC 254. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Dr. Rajkov. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Dr. Rajkov, I don't know whether I should start at all or not. We've got five minutes, but perhaps let us clarify some details.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters can not hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please briefly clarify part of your statement in writing that pertains to the conflict a few days before the 9th of May, 1993, and what you say about your hospital too, if I may jog your memory.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tell me what you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In your statement, you say that the war hospital was starting to work properly about a month before the conflict. "We were getting more and more material. The material was coming in from different sides. For the most part we got medical equipment from the former East German army." And then you say further on page 4 of the B/C/S text or, rather, page 3 of the English text: "Before the actual conflict we had a so-called test conflict period, the one I referred to a few -- a while ago." Tell us, what was this test conflict?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the period that people around me called test shooting, the test period, and later on that's what it was called. That's the way because "probna marisana" was the word used there. Later on it was called "marisana" in the jargon.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can we conclude that this test conflict was actually practice for a possible more extensive conflict where many more casualties can be expected?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that has nothing to do with my work and my hospital. I'm referring to the shooting during the night. During the day a member of the army and a member of the HVO would be sitting together and drinking Coca-Cola together, and at night they would shoot at each other.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: This pertains to the days before the 9th?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Your next sentence is: "During that time we were hosting Muslim doctors and nurses from the surgery didn't of the regional medical centre (HVO war hospital)." Tell us, please, in that period, was it noted that your colleagues of Muslim ethnicity from the war hospital of the HVO came to work in your hospital on the east bank?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a while before the 9th of May, if I can put it that way, that is what would correspond to the actual state of affairs. Sporadically, colleagues I knew from earlier on, surgeons, would come in to sort of be there to see what it looked like, because we had something there but it was not really our line of work, and they sort of told us what could be done. And there were a few surgical interventions that were carried out. I know that we operated on a soldier who was wounded a few days before the 9th of May. From my current point of view it was no major surgery but then it was pretty big and it couldn't have been done before that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did any of them bring any medical equipment or medicaments or anything else that would have been of assistance to you on the east bank?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, it's not that everyone brought something every time, but, yes, they did bring something. Sometimes some important thing would be lacking like, say, out of a set of instruments. If you look at it as a GP, you sort of thing oh, wonder of wonders, and then all of a sudden you see something is missing.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we just clarify a small inconsistency in what you were saying about your conversation to your commander on the 7th of May? Today Mr. Karnavas asked you where your commander was, and you said that you did not know roughly and that he phoned you and you didn't know where he was phoning you from. Yesterday, however, you said to us, and that was recorded in the transcript, that you called him only the 7th in the morning in order to report to him about what happened during your shift, and that is what you did customarily. Can you tell us now what this was all about?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's not waste energy on things that are not that important. This is what it was: With induction telephones you go to the signalman. You say call such-and-such a person. He says, "Wait, I need some time." And then they do this and that. I'm not very knowledgeable about these things it looks very primitive but it does require a certain procedure. So a sort of, you call and then he calls you. So I actually told the signalsman that he should call this number, a certain person, and that this person call me back as far as I know. I called and then I was called. I mean, both is correct. Of course it seems crazy now from the point of view of, say, cell phones.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: But it does know that you knew what number you were calling and you knew where the number was located and what building.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was no number. I would just say to the signalsman, "Call Ahmo." It's a small town. We all know each other. And he would call and then the other one would call me back..

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Dr. Rajkov, among your colleagues were there some that lived on the east bank, in view of the fact that you lived on the west bank? That's why I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell me, was the recommendation of your commander or your boss to remain on the east bank and to be in the hospital by way of a reserve? Did that pertain to your colleagues who lived on the east bank as well? Did they, just like you, stay on in the hospital during those days as a kind of reserve?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: It so happened, and that is how this was carried through, this advice, this recommendation of Dr. Ahmo. The next lady doctor who came stayed on. She lives on the east bank. The next doctor, I have to admit, did not follow the recommendation. He went home. He does live on the east bank but very far away, down south. He needed several days later on to get to the hospital and then the fourth one the next one was there. Yes, yes. Only the four of us. All of them live on the east bank.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let me just conclude. The recommendation pertained to those on the east bank as well; right?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the other doctors that I mentioned in -- they did not exist for us at the time.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers not speak at the same time, interpreters note.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it's beyond 7.00. I assume that we have to adjourn. I would have more questions of this witness, and I'm truly very sorry that we haven't got more time. If you allow me a few more minutes, some very brief clarifications --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you have five minutes for your clarifications.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now I'll be very brief I'm not going to go into any complex topics Dr. Rajkov you said to us today you heard the radio on the 9th of May calling upon members of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina to surrender and to hang out white flags. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I want to clarify this. It pertained to members of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: There wasn't any third party there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I see that you're surprised, but I am saying that you're the first witness who spoke of it in such terms because witnesses until now were telling us that this was directed at the Muslims to surrender. That's why I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can we also discuss the question of the ID that you had as far as back as 1992, because you lived on the west bank and there you needed an ID so that you could cross to the east bank at all. Tell us, if I remember what you said correctly, free passage to the east bank was allowed only to persons who lived there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who it was that issued such IDs to citizens in order to be able to cross over to the east bank?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who issued these documents to citizens so that they could cross over to the east bank so there would be proof that they really live on the east bank. I don't know because I lived on the west bank, so I wasn't really interested in that bit. Not to say how surprised I was when I was told that you -- you cannot go to the other side if you don't have an invitation or approval or whatever. And that's the way it was. A person I knew, an old person from Mostar, a disabled person, I got a document from him, a document making it possible for me to get there. It wasn't possible in any other way.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Dr. Rajkov, would it be right to conclude, then, that a Croat who lived on the west bank and who worked on the west bank could not get such an ID in order to cross to the other side because -- if there was no justification for crossing to the other side?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is quite possible, although I have the impression that there were yet other IDs that gave one the right to cross over, because a soldier could cross over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Doctor, we need a clarification at this point. We know that you were on the BiH side. We know that there was a front line. We know that you resided in West Mostar. When you went back home did you have to cross the front line and did you have to pass through check-points of the HVO and did you use your BiH ID?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, because the check-point existed at the old bridge and at the old bridge there were soldiers or policemen standing there, whatever they were, and to me they looked like soldiers of the BH army, although it seems to me that in a certain period of time the check-point was of mixed composition. There were HVO soldiers or policemen there. It varied. Sometimes both were there, yes. But as for another check-point, a purely HVO check-point, no. No, there wasn't one on the road from the old bridge to Dum where I lived, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we can conclude, then, that when you worked in the east part of Mostar you could move to go back home to the western part of Mostar, and you could again go back to work in the eastern part of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I could go and come back, up until the day of the conflict. That is to say, up until the date of the 6th I don't know after that up until then I could cross over, of course, with my ID.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Doctor, my colleagues are telling me that your answer to my question as to who issued IDs is not recorded in the transcript so could you please repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: You asked who issued IDs to cross over to the left bank or across the old bridge as we called it. I don't know who it was that issued the IDs because I didn't need to know anything about it because at the time I lived and worked on the west bank.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: This was an ID that said the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in my case. The paper I got as a basis in order to go there at all in terms of my activation as a physician in the BH army did have a letterhead stating the BH army and was signed by the commander of the 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really think that this is very important and when Judge Antonetti put the question, that is the line 17 -- sorry, 17, 5, said you got an ID from the BH had. As far as I heard Judge Antonetti, he said the army of the BH, not only of the BH.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Doctor, unfortunately I only have one more question and it has to do with the conflict itself on the 9th of May. Can you tell us whether the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina from its positions in the east part of Mostar shot at the west part of Mostar on that 9th of May, if you know about that?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis -- well, I only know on the basis of what I was told by the fighters who were from that area of the future separation line, those who would come to the institute as they were accompanying patients. Things were moving back and forth. Later they responded in fire as much as they could with what they had, and in terms of how many they were there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Doctor, do you know that already on the next day, the 10th of May, Alija Izetbegovic and Mate Boban agreed on a cease-fire and a truce? That two days later the commanders of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the HVO respectively agreed on a cessation of hostilities and a cease-fire?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know about that. I was never involved in higher levels then or now.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us about the 11th of May onwards up until mid-May or the end of May the conflicts were much -- of much, much lower intensity, and that they could not be compared to the intensity of the 9th and 10th of May?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN RAJKOV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, how should I put this? It was irregular. There was a curve and it went up and down. Sometimes more --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please not speak at the same time, interpreters note.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I'm interested in the first amplitude after the 10th of May?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic, you have to finish.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Should I answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you can answer very quickly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will. After the first crescendo I would have to say that it would own be logical to have a lull, lower intensity of gunfire. It seemed to me as an attempt to get something done. It didn't work, and now we're going to shoot at each other a bit. And then again every now and then, yes, well, the intensity went down after the original peak. As for the reason, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Doctor. On behalf of my colleagues I would like to thank you for coming to The Hague and having testified here. We have gone longer by 15 minutes, but it was very important to finish your testimony because of your profession, and for that reason we prolonged our session by 15 minutes, and the registrar will pardon me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And for next week we have nine witnesses. I hope we will arrive at hearing all of those nine witnesses, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We've plotted a course, Your Honours, and we'll do everything we can to get from A to B as quickly as possible. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have confidence in you. I would like to thank everybody, and I invite you all to come back on Monday at quarter past 2.00.
